title: What Is Fiber?
summary: Learn how fiber can carry information using light and connect networks across buildings and regions.
objectives: Explain at a high level how fiber carries information.
Distinguish a classroom fiber model from professional fiber work.

vocab.def: A thin strand that carries information using light.
The amount of information a connection can carry in a given time.
A connection between two points in a network.

sections.heading: Information can travel as light
sections.body: Fiber optic cables use light signals to carry information. Fiber links can move large amounts of information between networks, buildings, and regions.

sections.heading: A connection across distance
sections.body: Data centers depend on many links. Fiber may connect a facility to other networks, while other cables connect equipment inside it. Each link is part of a larger path.

sections.heading: Classroom model, professional boundary
sections.body: Use a drawing, yarn, or a light-and-card demonstration to model a link. Never look into a live fiber, handle glass fragments, use laser equipment, or operate a fusion splicer. Professional fiber work requires qualified supervision.

practice.prompt: Compare two paper network maps: one with a short link and one with a link between regions. What stays the same about the path, and what changes about its scale?

quiz.question: How does fiber carry information?
options: By removing the need for networks
By storing information in a rack label

reflectionPrompt: What question would you ask about the path information takes between two places?
